e: Yaakov sent messengers before him
to Eisov, his brother,
to the Land of Seir, to the field of Edom.
He commanded them saying,
This is what you should say
to my master, Eisov.
Your servant, Yaakov says,
I lived as a stranger with Lavan,
and was delayed until now.
I acquired oxen, donkeys,
sheep, servants and maidservants.
I have sent [these messengers] to tell my master,
to find favor in your eyes.
The messengers returned
to Yaakov saying,
We came to your brother, to Eisov,
and he is also coming to meet you;
and there are four hundred men with him.

h: וַיַּ֜חַץ אֶת־הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֗וֹ וְאֶת־הַצֹּ֧אן וְאֶת־הַבָּקָ֛ר וְהַגְּמַלִּ֖ים לִשְׁנֵ֥י מַחֲנֽוֹת׃
t: וּפַלֵּיג יָת עַמָּא דִי עִמֵּיהּ וְיָת עָנָא וְיָת תּוֹרֵי וְגַמְלַיָּא לִתְרֵין מַשִּׁירְיָן:
e: Yaakov was very frightened, and distressed.
He divided the people that were with him, along with the sheep, cattle and camels, into two camps.

h: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אִם־יָב֥וֹא עֵשָׂ֛ו אֶל־הַמַּחֲנֶ֥ה הָאַחַ֖ת וְהִכָּ֑הוּ
t: וַאֲמַר אִם יֵיתֵי עֵשָׂו לְמַשְׁרִיתָא חֲדָא וְיִמְחִנֵּיהּ
וִיהֵי (<small>נ"א</small> וְיִמְחֵנַהּ וּתְהִי) מַשְׁרִיתָא דְתִשְׁתָּאַר לְשֵׁיזָבָא:
e: He said, If Eisov comes to one camp and attacks it,
the remaining camp will survive.

h: יְהוָ֞ה הָאֹמֵ֣ר אֵלַ֗י שׁ֧וּב לְאַרְצְךָ֛ וּלְמוֹלַדְתְּךָ֖ וְאֵיטִ֥יבָה עִמָּֽךְ׃
t: יְיָ דִּי אֲמַר לִי תּוּב לְאַרְעָךְ וּלְיַלָּדוּתָךְ וְאוֹטֵיב עִמָּךְ:
e: Yaakov said,
God of my father Avraham,
and God of my father Yitzchok,
Adonoy Who said to me, Return to your land, to your birthplace, and I will do good with you.

t: אֲרֵי יְחִידִי עֲבָרִית יָת יַרְדְּנָא הָדֵין
e: I am unworthy [My merits are few] because of all the kindness and of all the faithfulness [goodness]
that you have done with Your servant;
for I crossed over this Jordan [only] with my staff [alone],
and now I have become two camps.

h: הַצִּילֵ֥נִי נָ֛א מִיַּ֥ד אָחִ֖י מִיַּ֣ד עֵשָׂ֑ו
e: Rescue me, I pray [now], from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Eisov,
for I fear him,
that he will come and attack me —
mother and children alike.
You have said,
I will do very good with you,
and I will make your offspring [many] like the sands of the sea,
which are too numerous to count.

h: וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִן־הַבָּ֧א בְיָד֛וֹ מִנְחָ֖ה לְעֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִֽיו׃
t: וּנְסִיב מִן דְּאַיְתִי בִידֵיהּ תִּקְרֻבְתָּא לְעֵשָׂו אֲחוּהִי:
e: He spent that night there.
He took from that which comes into his hand, [for] a present to his brother, Eisov.
Two hundred female goats
and twenty male goats,
two hundred ewes and twenty rams.
Thirty nursing camels and their young,
forty cows and ten bulls,
twenty female donkeys
and ten male donkeys.
He placed them in the hand of his servants,
each herd by itself.
He said to his servants, Pass on ahead of me,
and keep a space
between each herd.

h: כִּ֣י יִֽפְגָּשְׁךָ֞ עֵשָׂ֣ו אָחִ֗י וִשְׁאֵֽלְךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
t: אֲרֵי יְעַרְעִנָּךְ עֵשָׂו אָחִי וּשְׁאֵלִנָּךְ לְמֵימָר
e: He commanded the first one, saying,
When my brother, Eisov meets you and asks you saying,
To whom do you belong, and where are you going;
and who is the owner of this that is before you?
You should [then] say, [They belong] to your servant, Yaakov.
It is a present sent
to my master, Eisov,
and see, he is also [coming] behind us.

t: וּפַקִּיד אַף יָת תִּנְיָנָא אַף יָת תְּלִיתָאָה
אַף יָת כָּל דְּאָזְלִין בָּתַר עֲדָרַיָּא לְמֵימָר
e: He also commanded the second and also the third,
and to all who followed after the herds, saying,
In like manner must you speak to Eisov
when you find [meet] him.

h: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם גַּ֗ם הִנֵּ֛ה עַבְדְּךָ֥ יַעֲקֹ֖ב אַחֲרֵ֑ינוּ
כִּֽי־אָמַ֞ר אֲכַפְּרָ֣ה פָנָ֗יו בַּמִּנְחָה֙ הַהֹלֶ֣כֶת לְפָנָ֔י
t: וְתֵימְרוּן אַף הָא עַבְדָּךְ יַעֲקֹב אָתֵי בַתְרָנָא
אֲרֵי אֲמַר אַנְחִנֵּיהּ לְרוּגְזֵיהּ בְּתִקְרֻבְתָּא דְּאָזְלַת לָקֳדָמַי
e: You should also say, See, your servant Yaakov is [coming] behind us.
For he said, I will appease him [quieten his anger] with the present that goes before me,
and afterwards I will see his face,
perhaps he will forgive me.
The present passed on ahead of him,
but he spent the night in the camp.

h: וַיָּ֣קָם בַּלַּ֣יְלָה ה֗וּא וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־שְׁתֵּ֤י נָשָׁיו֙ וְאֶת־שְׁתֵּ֣י שִׁפְחֹתָ֔יו
t: וְקָם בְּלֵילְיָא הוּא וּדְבַר יָת תַּרְתֵּין נְשׁוֹהִי וְיָת תַּרְתֵּין לְחֵינָתֵיהּ
e: He got up that night and took his two wives, his two handmaids [concubines],
and his eleven children,
and crossed over the ford of the Yabbok [River].
He [then] took them and crossed them over the stream.
He [also] brought over all that he possessed.
Yaakov remained alone,
and a man wrestled with him
until daybreak.
He [the man] saw that he could not defeat him,
and he struck the socket [girth] of his hip.
[The girth of] Yaakov’s hip joint was dislocated
as he wrestled with him.
He [the man] said, Let me go,
for the dawn is breaking.
He [Yaakov] said, I will not let you go
unless you bless me.
He [the man] said to him, What is your name?
And he replied, Yaakov.

h: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֹ֤א יַעֲקֹב֙ יֵאָמֵ֥ר עוֹד֙ שִׁמְךָ֔
t: וַאֲמַר לָא יַעֲקֹב יִתְאֲמַר עוֹד שְׁמָךְ
אֲרֵי רַבְרְבַת קֳדָם יְיָ וְעִם גוּבְרַיָּא וִיכָלְתָּא:
e: He [the man] said, No longer will your name be spoken of as Yaakov,
but as Yisrael,
for you have contended with God[ly beings] [are great before God] and with men, and you have won.

t: וַאֲמַר לְמָה דְנַן אַתְּ שָׁאֵל לִשְׁמִי
e: Yaakov asked him, and said, Please [Now] tell me your name.
He said, Why then do you ask my name?
He then blessed him [Yaakov] there.
Yaakov named the place Peniel [God’s Face],
For I have seen God[ly beings] [Angles of God] face to face,
and my soul has survived.
The sun shone
for him as he passed by Penuel,
and he limped due to his hip.

h: עַל־כֵּ֡ן לֹֽא־יֹאכְל֨וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־גִּ֣יד הַנָּשֶׁ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־כַּ֣ף הַיָּרֵ֔ךְ
t: עַל כֵּן לָא יֵכְלוּן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יָת גִּידָא דְנַשְׁיָא דִּי עַל פְּתֵי יַרְכָּא
e: Therefore, the children of Israel must not eat the displaced tendon [nerve] which is on the [girth of the] hip joint
to this very day;
because he struck [the girth of] Yaakov’s hip joint
on the displaced tendon.

h: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א יַעֲקֹ֜ב עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּרְא֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה עֵשָׂ֣ו בָּ֔א
t: וּזְקַף יַעֲקֹב עֵינוֹהִי וַחֲזָא וְהָא עֵשָׂו אֲתָא
וּפַלִּיג יָת בְּנַיָּא עַל לֵאָה וְעַל רָחֵל
e: Yaakov raised his eyes and saw that Eisov was coming,
and with him there were four hundred men.
He then divided the children among Leah, Rochel
and the two handmaids [concubines].
He placed the handmaids [concubines] and their children foremost,
Leah and her sons behind them,
and Rochel and Yoseif in the rear.
He went ahead of them,
and he prostrated himself to the earth seven times,
until he approached his brother.
Eisov ran to meet him. He hugged him
and fell on his neck and kissed him.
They [both] wept.

t: וּזְקַף יָת עֵינוֹהִי וַחֲזָא יָת נְשַׁיָּא וְיָת בְּנַיָּא
e: [Eisov] raised his eyes and saw the women and children.
He said, Who are these to you?
He [Yaakov] said, These are the children
whom God has graciously [compassionately] granted your servant.
The handmaids [concubines] [then] approached, they, and their children, and prostrated themselves.

t: וּבָתַר כֵּן קְרֵיב יוֹסֵף וְרָחֵל וּסְגִידוּ:
e: Leah and her children also approached and prostrated themselves,
and finally Yoseif and Rochel approached and prostrated themselves.

h: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֥י לְךָ֛ כָּל־הַמַּחֲנֶ֥ה הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּגָ֑שְׁתִּי
t: וַאֲמַר מָן לָךְ כָּל מַשְׁרִיתָא הָדֵין דִּי עֲרָעִית
e: He [Eisov] said, What do you have to do with that whole camp that approached me?
He [Yaakov] said, It was to find favor in the eyes of my master.
Eisov said, I have plenty.
My brother, let what you have remain yours [be successful].

h: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֗ב אַל־נָא֙ אִם־נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ
כִּ֣י עַל־כֵּ֞ן רָאִ֣יתִי פָנֶ֗יךָ כִּרְאֹ֛ת פְּנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים וַתִּרְצֵֽנִי׃
t: וַאֲמַר יַעֲקֹב בְּבָעוּ אִם כְּעַן אַשְׁכָּחִית רַחֲמִין בְּעֵינָיךְ
אֲרֵי עַל כֵּן חֲזִתִּנּוּן לְאַפָּיךְ כְּחֵיזוּ אַפֵּי רַבְרְבַיָּא וְאִתְרְעֵית לִי:
e: Yaakov said, Please, no. If I have found favor in your eyes [now],
take [accept] my present from my hand,
because I have seen your face [and it was] like seeing the face of a God[ly being] [great ones]; and you have received me favorably.

t: אֲרֵי רַחִים עֲלַי (קֳדָם) יְיָ וַאֲרֵי אִית לִי כֹלָּא
e: Please [Now] accept my blessing [present] as it was brought to you,
for God has been gracious to me, for I have everything.
He thus urged him and he took [accepted] it.
He [Eisov] said, Go and we will move on,
and I will move on with you.

h: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו אֲדֹנִ֤י יֹדֵ֙עַ֙ כִּֽי־הַיְלָדִ֣ים רַכִּ֔ים
t: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רִבּוֹנִי יְדַע אֲרֵי יָנְקַיָּא רַכִּיכִין
e: He [Yaakov] said to him, My master knows that the children are delicate,
and that the sheep and cattle with me are nursing.
If they are driven hard for [even] one day,
all the sheep will die.

h: וַאֲנִ֞י אֶֽתְנָהֲלָ֣ה לְאִטִּ֗י לְרֶ֨גֶל הַמְּלָאכָ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־לְפָנַי֙ וּלְרֶ֣גֶל הַיְלָדִ֔ים
t: וַאֲנָא אֱדַבֵּר בְּנִיחַ לְרֶגֶל עוֹבַדְתָּא דִי קֳדָמַי וּלְרֶגֶל יָנְקַיָּא
עַד דִּי אֵעוֹל לְוַת רִבּוֹנִי לְשֵׂעִיר:
e: Please [Now] my master, go on ahead of your servant.
I will lead on gently, in my slow pace, according to the pace of the work that is before me, and according to the pace of the children,
until I come to my master in Seir.
Eisov said,
Let me leave [now] with you
some of the people that are with me.
He [Yaakov] said, What for?
Let me find favor in the eyes of my master.

h: וַיָּשָׁב֩ בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֥וּא עֵשָׂ֛ו לְדַרְכּ֖וֹ שֵׂעִֽירָה׃
t: וְתָב בְּיוֹמָא הַהוּא עֵשָׂו לְאָרְחֵיהּ לְשֵׂעִיר:
e: On that day Eisov returned on his way—going to Seir.

t: עַל כֵּן קְרָא שְׁמָא דְאַתְרָא סֻכּוֹת:
e: Yaakov traveled to Sukkos
and built himself a house,
and for his livestock he made shelters.
He therefore named the place Sukkos.

h: וַיָּבֹא֩ יַעֲקֹ֨ב שָׁלֵ֜ם עִ֣יר שְׁכֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן
t: וַאֲתָא יַעֲקֹב שְׁלִים קַרְתָּא דִשְׁכֶם דִּי בְּאַרְעָא דִכְנָעַן
e: Yaakov arrived safely at the city of Shechem, which is in the Land of Canaan,
when he came from Padan Aram.
He encamped before the city.

h: וַיִּ֜קֶן אֶת־חֶלְקַ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽטָה־שָׁם֙ אָהֳל֔וֹ
t: וּזְבַן יָת אַחֲסָנַת חַקְלָא דִּי פְרַס תַּמָּן מַשְׁכְּנֵיהּ
e: He bought the part [possession] of the field where he had spread his tent,
from the sons of Chamor, father of Shechem,
for one hundred kesitahs [sheep].
He erected an altar there
and called it [worshiped upon it before] the Almighty is [the] God of Yisrael.
Deenah went out, the daughter of Leah,
whom she had borne to Yaakov,
to see [visit] the local girls.

h: וַיַּ֨רְא אֹתָ֜הּ שְׁכֶ֧ם בֶּן־חֲמ֛וֹר הַֽחִוִּ֖י נְשִׂ֣יא הָאָ֑רֶץ
t: וַחֲזָא יָתַהּ שְׁכֶם בַּר חֲמוֹר חִיוָאָה רַבָּא דְאַרְעָא
e: She was seen by Shechem, son of Chamor, the Chivite, who was the prince of the land.
He took her, was with her, and mistreated her.
He became deeply attached to [He desired]
Deenah, the daughter of Yaakov,
and he loved the girl.
He spoke to the girl’s heart.

t: סַב לִי יָת עוּלֶמְתָּא הָדָא לְאִנְתּוּ:
e: Shechem spoke to his father Chamor, saying,
Take this young girl for me as a wife.

h: וְיַעֲקֹ֣ב שָׁמַ֗ע כִּ֤י טִמֵּא֙ אֶת־דִּינָ֣ה בִתּ֔וֹ
t: וְיַעֲקֹב שְׁמַע אֲרֵי סָאֵיב יָת דִּינָה בְרַתֵּיהּ
e: Yaakov heard that he had defiled his daughter, Deenah,
[while] his sons were with the livestock in the fields.
Yaakov remained silent until they returned.

t: וּנְפַק חֲמוֹר אֲבוּהִי דִשְׁכֶם לְוַת יַעֲקֹב
e: Chamor, father of Shechem, went out to Yaakov
to speak with him.

t: וּבְנֵי יַעֲקֹב עַלּוּ מִן חַקְלָא כַּד שְׁמָעוּ
אֲרֵי קְלָנָא עֲבַד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְמִשְׁכַּב עִם בַּת יַעֲקֹב
e: The sons of Yaakov returned from the field when they heard [what had happened].
The men grieved
and were very angry,
for he [Shechem] had committed an outrage against Yisrael to lie with a daughter of Yaakov.
Such a thing should not be done [It is not fitting for such a think to have been done].
Chamor spoke with them saying,
My son, Shechem, desires your daughter.
Please [Now] grant her to him for a wife.
Intermarry with us.
Give us your daughters,
and take our daughters for yourselves.
You will [then] live with us
and the land will be open to you.
Live and [do] trade in [with] it
and possess it.
Shechem said to her father and her brothers,
Let me find favor in your eyes
and what ever you say [ask of me], I will give.
Increase greatly the amount I must pay for the bridal dowry and gifts.
I will give whatever you say,
but give me the girl for a wife.

h: וַיַּעֲנ֨וּ בְנֵֽי־יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶת־שְׁכֶ֨ם וְאֶת־חֲמ֥וֹר אָבִ֛יו בְּמִרְמָ֖ה וַיְדַבֵּ֑רוּ
t: וַאֲתִיבוּ בְנֵי יַעֲקֹב יָת שְׁכֶם וְיָת חֲמוֹר אֲבוּהִי בְּחָכְמָתָא וּמַלִּילוּ
e: The sons of Yaakov answered Shechem, and his father Chamor, with guile [cleverness], when they spoke;
because he had defiled their sister, Deenah.

h: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם לֹ֤א נוּכַל֙ לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה
t: וַאֲמָרוּ לְהוֹן לָא נִכּוּל לְמֶעְבַּד פִּתְגָּמָא הָדֵין
e: They said to them, We cannot do such a thing —
to give our sister
[in marriage] to an uncircumcised man,
for that is a disgrace to us.
This is the only way we will consent to you:
if you will be like us,
circumcising all your males.
[Then] we will give our daughters to you,
and we will take your daughters for ourselves.
We will live together with you,
and we will become one people.
But if you do not listen to [obey] us to be circumcised,
we will take our daughter and go.
Their words were agreeable in the eyes of Chamor,
and in the eyes of Shechem, the son of Chamor.
The young man did not delay doing the thing,
because he desired the daughter of Yaakov.
He was the most honored person in his father’s house.

h: וַיָּבֹ֥א חֲמ֛וֹר וּשְׁכֶ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ אֶל־שַׁ֣עַר עִירָ֑ם
t: וַאֲתָא חֲמוֹר וּשְׁכֶם בְּרֵיהּ לִתְרַע קַרְתְּהוֹן
e: Chamor and his son, Shechem came to the gate of their city,
and they spoke to the men of their city saying,

h: הָאֲנָשִׁ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה שְֽׁלֵמִ֧ים הֵ֣ם אִתָּ֗נוּ וְיֵשְׁב֤וּ בָאָ֙רֶץ֙ וְיִסְחֲר֣וּ אֹתָ֔הּ
t: גֻּבְרַיָּא הָאִלֵּין שָׁלְמִין אִנּוּן עִמָּנָא וִיתִיבוּן בְּאַרְעָא וְיַעְבְּדוּן בַּהּ סְחוֹרְתָא
e: These men are completely at peace with us. Let them live in the land and [do] trade in [with] it.
The land has ample room to be open to them.
We will take their daughters for wives,
and we will give them our daughters.

h: אַךְ־בְּ֠זֹאת יֵאֹ֨תוּ לָ֤נוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים֙ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת אִתָּ֔נוּ
t: בְּרַם בְּדָא יִתָּפְסוּן לָנָא גוּבְרַיָּא לְמִתַּב עִמָּנָא
e: But only on these terms will the men consent to live with us,
to become one people:
every male among us must be circumcised,
just as they are circumcised.
Their livestock, their possessions and all their cattle,
will it not be ours?
Only let us consent to them,
and they will live with us.
They listened to [obeyed] Chamor, and to his son, Shechem —
all those who passed through the gate of his city.
Every male was circumcised —
all who passed through the gate of his city.

h: וַיְהִי֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֜י בִּֽהְיוֹתָ֣ם כֹּֽאֲבִ֗ים וַיִּקְח֣וּ שְׁנֵֽי־בְנֵי־יַ֠עֲקֹב שִׁמְע֨וֹן וְלֵוִ֜י אֲחֵ֤י דִינָה֙ אִ֣ישׁ חַרְבּ֔וֹ
t: וַהֲוָה בְיוֹמָא תְלִיתָאָה כַּד תְּקִיפוּ עֲלֵיהוֹן כֵּאבֵיהוֹן וּנְסִיבוּ תְרֵין בְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב שִׁמְעוֹן וְלֵוִי אֲחֵי דִינָה גְּבַר חַרְבֵּיהּ
e: On the third day when they were in pain [their pain was strong upon them], two of Yaakov’s sons, Shimon and Leivi, brothers of Deenah, each took his sword.
They approached the city with confidence [whose inhabitants dwell in security],
and killed every male.

t: וּדְבָרוּ יָת דִּינָה מִבֵּית שְׁכֶם וּנְפָקוּ:
e: They killed Chamor and his son Shechem
at the point of the sword.
They took Deenah from the house of Shechem and they left.
The sons of Yaakov came upon the corpses [to strip the corpses],
and they plundered the city
that had defiled their sister.

t: יָת עָנְהוֹן וְיָת תּוֹרְהוֹן וְיָת חֲמָרֵיהוֹן
וְיָת דִּי בְקַרְתָּא וְיָת דִּי בְחַקְלָא בְּזוֹ (ס"א דְבָרוּ):
e: Their sheep, their cattle, their donkeys,
whatever was in the city and whatever was in the field—they took [plundered].

t: וְיָת כָּל נִכְסֵיהוֹן וְיָת כָּל טַפְלְהוֹן וְיָת נְשֵׁיהוֹן
e: All their wealth, all their children, and their wives —
they took captive, and plundered —
including everything in the houses.

h: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶל־שִׁמְע֣וֹן וְאֶל־לֵוִי֮ עֲכַרְתֶּ֣ם אֹתִי֒
t: וַאֲמַר יַעֲקֹב לְשִׁמְעוֹן וּלְלֵוִי עֲכַרְתּוּן יָתִי
e: Yaakov said to Shimon and Leivi, You have made trouble for me,
making me obnoxious to [putting hatred between us and] the inhabitants of the land,
the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
[Since] I am few in number,
they will gather together and attack me.
I and my house [family] will be destroyed.
They said,
Should he make our sister [be treated] into a harlot [like one who goes outside]?

t: קוּם סַק לְבֵית אֵל וְתִיב תַּמָּן
e: Elohim said to Yaakov,
Arise, go up to Beis Eil and live there;
make an altar there
to the Almighty Who appeared [became revealed] to you
when you were fleeing from your brother Eisov.
Yaakov [then] said to his household,
and to everyone that was with him,
Get rid of the foreign gods [false gods of the nations] in your midst.
Purify yourselves and change your garments.

h: וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה־שָּׁ֣ם מִזְבֵּ֗חַ לָאֵ֞ל הָעֹנֶ֤ה אֹתִי֙ בְּי֣וֹם צָֽרָתִ֔י
t: וְאֶעְבֵּד תַּמָּן מַדְבְּחָא לֵאלָהָא דְּקַבֵּל צְלוֹתִי בְּיוֹמָא דְעַקְתִי
e: Let us arise and go up to Beis Eil.
There I will make an altar to the Almighty, Who answered me [accepted my prayer] in the day of my distress,
and Who was with me [whose Word was my support]
along the way I traveled.

h: וַיִּתְּנ֣וּ אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֗ב אֵ֣ת כָּל־אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַנֵּכָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָדָ֔ם
t: וִיהָבוּ לְיַעֲקֹב יָת כָּל טַעֲוַת עַמְמַיָּא דִי בִידֵיהוֹן
e: They gave Yaakov all the foreign gods [false gods of the nations] that were in their hands,
and [also] the rings in their ears.
Yaakov buried them
under the oak [tree] which was near Shechem.

h: וַיְהִ֣י חִתַּ֣ת אֱלֹהִ֗ים עַל־הֶֽעָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ סְבִיבֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם
t: וַהֲוַת דַּחֲלָא דַיְיָ עַל עַמְמַיָּא דִּי בְּקִרְוֵי סַחֲרָנֵיהוֹן
e: They began their journey.
The terror of Elohim was upon the [people who were in the] cities that were around them,
and they did not pursue the sons of Yaakov.

h: וַיָּבֹ֨א יַעֲקֹ֜ב ל֗וּזָה אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן
t: וַאֲתָא יַעֲקֹב לְלוּז דִּי בְּאַרְעָא דִכְנַעַן
e: Yaakov came to Luz, which was in the land of Canaan —
that is, to Beis Eil —
he and all the people that were with him.
There he built an altar,
and he called the place
Eil Beis Eil,
for there Elohim was revealed to him
when he was fleeing from his brother.
Devorah, Rivkah’s nurse, died,
and she was buried below Beis Eil, under Allon [on the lower plain].
He named it Allon of Weeping [Plain of the Weeping].
Elohim again appeared [became revealed] to Yaakov
when he came from Padan Aram,
and He blessed him.

h: לֹֽא־יִקָּרֵא֩ שִׁמְךָ֨ ע֜וֹד יַעֲקֹ֗ב כִּ֤י אִם־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׁמֶ֔ךָ
t: לָא יִתְקְרֵי שְׁמָךְ עוֹד יַעֲקֹב אֶלָּהֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל יְהֵא שְׁמָךְ
e: Elohim said to him. Your name is Yaakov.
No longer will your name be Yaakov, but Yisrael will be your name;
and He named him Yisrael.

h: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֲנִ֨י אֵ֤ל שַׁדַּי֙ פְּרֵ֣ה וּרְבֵ֔ה
t: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ יְיָ אֲנָא אֵל שַׁדַּי פּוּשׁ וּסְגֵי
e: Elohim said to him, I am Almighty Shaddai. Be fruitful and increase,
a nation and a community of nations [an assembly of tribes] will come from you,
and kings [who rule over nations] will come out of your loins [descend from you].

h: וְאֶת־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֛תִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם וּלְיִצְחָ֖ק לְךָ֣ אֶתְּנֶ֑נָּה
t: וְיָת אַרְעָא דִּי יְהָבִית לְאַבְרָהָם וּלְיִצְחָק לָךְ אֶתְּנִנַהּ
e: The land that I gave to Avraham and Yitzchok, I will give to you;
and to your offspring after you I will give the land.
[The Glory of] Elohim ascended from him
at the place where He had spoken to him.

h: וַיַּצֵּ֨ב יַעֲקֹ֜ב מַצֵּבָ֗ה בַּמָּק֛וֹם אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ מַצֶּ֣בֶת אָ֑בֶן
t: וַאֲקֵים יַעֲקֹב קַמְתָא בְּאַתְרָא דִּי מַלִּיל עִמֵּיהּ קָמַת אַבְנָא
e: Yaakov set up a monument in the place where He had spoken to him, it was a monument of [a single] stone.
He poured a libation [libations] on it,
and he [also] poured oil on it.

h: וַיִּקְרָ֨א יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבֶּ֨ר אִתּ֥וֹ שָׁ֛ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים בֵּֽית־אֵֽל׃
t: וּקְרָא יַעֲקֹב יָת שְׁמָא דְאַתְרָא דִּי מַלִּיל עִמֵּיהּ תַּמָּן יְיָ בֵּית אֵל:
e: Yaakov named the place where Elohim had spoken to him; Beis Eil, [the House of the Almighty].

t: וַהֲוָה עוֹד כְּרוּבַת אַרְעָא לְמֵיעַל לְאֶפְרָת
e: They journeyed on from Beis Eil,
and there was yet a stretch of land before [they would reach] Ephros
when Rochel began to give birth. Her labor was very difficult.
When her labor was at its most difficult stage,
the midwife said to her, Do not fear,
for this one will also be a son for you.

t: וַהֲוָה בְּמִפַּק נַפְשַׁהּ אֲרֵי מִיתַת (<small>נ"א</small> מַיְתָא)
e: As her soul was departing, for she died,
she named him Ben Oni [son of my sorrow],
but his father named him Binyomin.
Rochel died
and was buried on the way to Ephros,
which is Beis Lechem [Bethlehem].

t: הִיא קָמַת קְבֻרְתָּא דְרָחֵל עַד יוֹמָא דֵין:
e: Yaakov set up a monument on her grave.
This monument is on Rochel’s grave to this very day.
Yisrael traveled on,
and set up [spread] his tent
beyond Migdal Eider [Tower of the herds].

t: וַהֲוָה כַּד שְׁרָא יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאַרְעָא הַהִיא
e: When Yaakov was settled in that land.
Reuvein went
and lay near Bilhah, his father’s concubine,
and Yisrael heard [about it].
The sons of Yaakov were twelve.
The sons of Leah [were]:
Reuvein, Yaakov’s firstborn,
Shimon, Leivi, Yehudah,
Yissachar and Zevulun.
The sons of Rochel [were]:
Yoseif and Binyomin.
The sons of Bilhah, Rochel’s handmaid, [were]:
Don and Naftali.

h: וּבְנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֛ה שִׁפְחַ֥ת לֵאָ֖ה גָּ֣ד וְאָשֵׁ֑ר
t: וּבְנֵי זִלְפָּה אַמְתָא דְלֵאָה גָּד וְאָשֵׁר
e: The sons of Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid, [were]: Gad and Asher.
These are the sons of Yaakov
that were born to him in Padan Aram.
Yaakov came to Yitzchok, his father,
in Mamrei at Kiryas Arba,
which is Chevron
where Avraham and Yitzchok lived.
The days of [the life of] Yitzchok
were one hundred and eighty years.
Yitzchok expired and died. He was gathered to his people
old and in the fullness of days.
His sons, Eisov and Yaakov buried him.
These are the descendants of Eisov, also known as Edom.

t: עֵשָׂו נְסִיב יָת נְשׁוֹהִי מִבְּנַת כְּנָעַן
e: Eisov took his wives from the daughters of Canaan:
Adah, the daughter of Eylon, the Chittite,
and Oholivomoh, the daughter of Anoh,
daughter of Tzivon, the Chivite.

t: וְיָת בָּשְׂמַת בַּת יִשְׁמָעֵאל אֲחָתֵיהּ דִּנְבָיוֹת:
e: [He also took] Bosmas, the daughter of Yishmael, the sister of Nevayos.
Adah bore to Eisov, [his son] Eliphaz,
and Bosmas bore Reueil.

t: יָת יְעוּשׁ וְיָת יַעְלָם וְיָת קֹרַח
e: Oholivomoh bore
Yeush, Yalom, and Korach.
These are the sons of Eisov
that were born to him in the land of Canaan.

h: וַיִּקַּ֣ח עֵשָׂ֡ו אֶת־נָ֠שָׁיו וְאֶת־בָּנָ֣יו וְאֶת־בְּנֹתָיו֮ וְאֶת־כָּל־נַפְשׁ֣וֹת בֵּיתוֹ֒
t: וּדְבַר עֵשָׂו יָת נְשׁוֹהִי וְיָת בְּנוֹהִי וְיָת בְּנָתֵיהּ וְיָת כָּל נַפְשַׁת בֵּיתֵיהּ
וְיָת גֵּיתוֹהִי וְיָת כָּל בְּעִירֵיהּ וְיָת כָּל קִנְיָנֵיהּ
e: Eisov took his wives, his sons, his daughters, all the people of his household,
his livestock, all his animals, and all his possessions
that he had acquired in the land of Canaan,
and he went to a [different] land
away from his brother, Yaakov.

h: וְלֹ֨א יָֽכְלָ֜ה אֶ֤רֶץ מְגֽוּרֵיהֶם֙ לָשֵׂ֣את אֹתָ֔ם
t: אֲרֵי הֲוָה קִנְיָנְהוֹן סַגִּי מִלְּמִתַּב כַּחֲדָא
וְלָא יְכִילַת אֲרַע תּוֹתָבוּתְהוֹן לְסוֹבָרָא יָתְהוֹן
e: For their wealth was too great for them to live together.
The land in which they lived temporarily could not support them
because of their livestock.
Eisov [therefore] settled in Mount Seir.
Eisov is Edom.
These are the descendants of Eisov, the ancestor of Edom
[the Edomites] in Mount Seir.
These are the names of Eisov’s sons:
Eliphaz, the son of Adah, the wife of Eisov,
Reueil, the son of Bosmas, the wife of Eisov.
The sons of Eliphaz were
Teiman, Omar,
Tzepho, Gatam and Kenaz.

t: וְתִמְנַע הֲוַת לְחֵינָתָא לֶאֱלִיפַז בַּר עֵשָׂו
e: Timna became a concubine to Eliphaz, Eisov’s son,
and she bore to Eliphaz [a son], Amaleik.
These are the sons of Adah, the wife of Eisov.

h: אֵ֣לֶּ֣ה הָי֔וּ בְּנֵ֥י בָשְׂמַ֖ת אֵ֥שֶׁת עֵשָֽׂו׃
t: אִלֵּין הֲווֹ בְּנֵי בָשְׂמַת אִתַּת עֵשָׂו:
e: These are the sons of Reueil,
Nachas, Zerach, Shamoh, and Mizzoh.
These were the sons of Bosmas, the wife of Eisov.

h: וְאֵ֣לֶּה הָי֗וּ בְּנֵ֨י אָהֳלִיבָמָ֧ה בַת־עֲנָ֛ה בַּת־צִבְע֖וֹן אֵ֣שֶׁת עֵשָׂ֑ו
t: וְאִלֵּין הֲווֹ בְּנֵי אָהֳלִיבָמָה בַת עֲנָה בַּת צִבְעוֹן אִתַּת עֵשָׂו
יָת יְעוּשׁ וְיָת יַעְלָם וְיָת קֹרַח:
e: These are the sons of Oholivomoh, the daughter of Anoh, the daughter of Tzivon, the wife of Eisov;
she bore to Eisov:
Ye’ush, Yalom and Korach.
These are the chiefs of the sons of Eisov:
the sons of Eliphaz, Eisov’s first born:
Chief Teiman, Chief Omar,
Chief Tzepho, Chief Kenaz.

t: רַבָּא קֹרַח רַבָּא גַעְתָּם רַבָּא עֲמָלֵק
e: Chief Korach, Chief Gatam, Chief Amaleik.
These are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom.
These are the sons of Adah.
These are the sons of Reu’eil, Eisov’s son:
Chief Nachas, Chief Zerach.
Chief Shamoh, Chief Mizzoh.
These are the Chiefs of Reu’eil in the land of Edom.
These are sons of Bosmas, wife of Eisov.

h: אַלּ֥וּף יְע֛וּשׁ אַלּ֥וּף יַעְלָ֖ם אַלּ֣וּף קֹ֑רַח
אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֞י אָֽהֳלִיבָמָ֛ה בַּת־עֲנָ֖ה אֵ֥שֶׁת עֵשָֽׂו׃
t: רַבָּא יְעוּשׁ רַבָּא יַעְלָם רַבָּא קֹרַח
אִלֵּין רַבְרְבֵי אָהֳלִיבָמָה בַּת עֲנָה אִתַּת עֵשָׂו:
e: These are the sons of Oholivomoh, wife of Eisov:
Chief Ye’ush, Chief Yalom, Chief Korach.
These are the Chiefs of Oholivomoh, daughter of Anoh, wife of Eisov.

h: אֵ֧לֶּה בְנֵי־עֵשָׂ֛ו וְאֵ֥לֶּה אַלּוּפֵיהֶ֖ם ה֥וּא אֱדֽוֹם׃
t: אִלֵּין בְּנֵי עֵשָׂו וְאִלֵּין רַבְרְבָנֵיהוֹן הוּא אֱדוֹם:
e: These are the sons of Eisov, and these are their chiefs, he is Edom.
These are the sons of Se’ir, the Chorite,
the inhabitants of the land:
Lotan, Shoval, Tzivon, and Anoh.

h: אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֧י הַחֹרִ֛י בְּנֵ֥י שֵׂעִ֖יר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אֱדֽוֹם׃
t: אִלֵּין רַבְרְבֵי חוֹרָאֵי בְּנֵי שֵׂעִיר בְּאַרְעָא דֶאֱדוֹם:
e: Dishon, Eitzer and Dishan,
these are the chiefs of the Chorites, the sons of Se’ir, in the land of Edom.
The sons of Lotan were Chori and Heimam.
Lotan’s sister was Timna.
These are the sons of Shoval:
Alvan, Manachas, Eival,
Shefo and Onom.

h: ה֣וּא עֲנָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָצָ֤א אֶת־הַיֵּמִם֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר
t: הוּא עֲנָה דִּי אַשְׁכַּח יָת גִּבָּרַיָּא בְּמַדְבְּרָא
כַּד הֲוָה רָעֵי יָת חֲמָרַיָּא לְצִבְעוֹן אֲבוּהִי:
e: These are the sons of Tzivon: Ayoh and Anoh.
He is the same Anoh who found the mules [mighty ones] in the desert
while tending the donkeys for his father, Tzivon.
These are the children of Anoh: Dishon,
and Oholivomoh the daughter of Anoh.
These are the sons of Dishon:
Chemdan, Eshban, Yisran and Keran.
These are the sons of Eitzer:
Bilhan, Za’avan and Akan.
These are the sons of Dishon: Utz and Aran.
These are the chiefs of the Chorites:
Chief Lotan, Chief Shoval,
Chief Tzivon, Chief Anoh.

h: אַלּ֥וּף דִּשֹׁ֛ן אַלּ֥וּף אֵ֖צֶר אַלּ֣וּף דִּישָׁ֑ן
אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֧י הַחֹרִ֛י לְאַלֻּפֵיהֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ שֵׂעִֽיר׃
t: רַבָּא דִשֹׁן רַבָּא אֵצֶר רַבָּא דִישָׁן
אִלֵּין רַבְרְבֵי חוֹרָאָה לְרַבְרְבָנֵיהוֹן בְּאַרְעָא דְשֵׂעִיר:
e: Chief Dishon, Chief Eitzer, Chief Dishan.
These are the chiefs of the Chorites based on the ranks of chiefs in the Land of Se’ir.

t: קֳדָם דִּי מְלַךְ מַלְכָּא לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל:
e: These are the kings
who reigned in the Land of Edom
before any king reigned over the Children of Israel.
Bela, son of Be’or reigned in Edom,
and the name of his city was Dinhavah.
Bela died,
and he was succeeded as king
by Yovav, son of Zerach, from Botzroh.
Yovav died,
and he was succeeded as king
by Chusham from the land of the Teimanites [South].

h: וַיִּמְלֹ֨ךְ תַּחְתָּ֜יו הֲדַ֣ד בֶּן־בְּדַ֗ד הַמַּכֶּ֤ה אֶת־מִדְיָן֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה מוֹאָ֔ב
t: וּמְלַךְ תְּחוֹתוֹהִי הֲדַד בַּר בְּדַד דִּקְטִיל יָת מִדְיָנָאֵי בְּחַקְלָא דְמוֹאָב
e: Chusham died,
and he was succeeded as king by Hadad, son of Bedad, who attacked [killed] Midian [the Midianites] in the field of Moav,
and the name of his city was Avis.
Hadad died,
and he was succeeded as king
by Samlah of Masriekah.
Samlah died,
and he was succeeded as king
by Sha’ul from Rechovos-by-the-river [P’ras].
Sha’ul died,
and he was succeeded as king
by Ba’al-Chanan, son of Achbor.
Ba’al-Chanan, son of Achbor died,
and he was succeeded as king by Hadar.
The name of his city was Pa’u.
His wife’s name was Meheitaveil, the daughter of Matreid,
daughter of Mei-Zahav [a goldsmith].

h: אַלּ֥וּף תִּמְנָ֛ע אַלּ֥וּף עַֽלְוָ֖ה אַלּ֥וּף יְתֵֽת׃
t: רַבָּא תִמְנָע רַבָּא עַלְוָה רַבָּא יְתֵת:
e: These are the names of the chiefs of Eisov, each with their families,
according to their places, by their names:
Chief Timna, Chief Alvoh, Chief Yeseis.

h: אַלּ֧וּף אָהֳלִיבָמָ֛ה אַלּ֥וּף אֵלָ֖ה אַלּ֥וּף פִּינֹֽן׃
t: רַבָּא אָהֳלִיבָמָה רַבָּא אֵלָה רַבָּא פִינֹן:
e: Chief Oholivomoh, Chief Eilah, Chief Pinon.

h: אַלּ֥וּף קְנַ֛ז אַלּ֥וּף תֵּימָ֖ן אַלּ֥וּף מִבְצָֽר׃
t: רַבָּא קְנַז רַבָּא תֵימָן רַבָּא מִבְצָר:
e: Chief Kenaz, Chief Teimon, Chief Mivtzar.

h: אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֣י אֱד֗וֹם לְמֹֽשְׁבֹתָם֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אֲחֻזָּתָ֔ם
t: אִלֵּין רַבְרְבֵי אֱדוֹם לְמוֹתְבָנְהוֹן בְּאַרְעָא אַחֲסַנְתְּהוֹן
e: Chief Magdiel, Chief Iram.
These are the chiefs of Edom according to their places of residence, in the land of their possession.
Thus was Eisov the ancestor of the Edomites.
